description: Moving between images, regions, meshes and 3D file formats, preparing solids for 3D printing, and converting geometry into printable or renderable form.

tools.name: Printout3D
tools.description: Prepares a 3D model for printing and sends it to a local printer, a file or an online printing service. It repairs, scales and orients the geometry as needed. Use it as the final step of a 3D printing workflow.

parameters.name: RegionSize
parameters.description: Physical size of the printed object, as a Quantity.

parameters.name: "ModelOrientation"
parameters.description: How the model is oriented on the print bed.

tools.notes: Models must be watertight; use RepairMesh on imported geometry before printing.

tools.name: RepairMesh
tools.description: Fixes defects in a mesh region such as holes, self-intersections, duplicate vertices and flipped normals. Which defect types to repair can be specified. Use it on imported STL or scanned geometry before measurement or printing.

tools.name: RegionImage
tools.description: Rasterizes a geometric region into an Image or Image3D of voxels. It is the bridge from exact geometry back into the image world. Use it for voxelization, mask generation and image-based analysis of shapes.
tools.notes: ImageMesh performs the inverse conversion from image to region.

tools.name: ImageMesh
tools.description: Converts the foreground of a binary image, or the voxels of an Image3D, into a MeshRegion. The result supports exact geometric operations such as Area, Volume and boolean combination. Use it to turn segmentation results into geometry.

tools.name: BoundaryMesh
tools.description: Converts a mesh region or other geometry into a BoundaryMeshRegion describing only its boundary surface. This is the representation that STL and most 3D printing workflows expect. Use it before exporting solids.

tools.name: RegionResize
tools.description: Scales a region to a given size or by a given factor, optionally per axis. It preserves the geometry type where possible. Use it to set physical dimensions before export or printing.

tools.name: Image3DSlices
tools.description: Extracts 2D slices from a 3D voxel image along a chosen direction. It is the standard way to inspect volumetric data slice by slice. Specific slice indices or a count can be requested.
tools.usage:
Image3DSlices[image3D]
Image3DSlices[image3D, n]
Image3DSlices[image3D, slices, dir]

tools.name: MeshRegionQ
tools.description: Tests whether an expression is a valid MeshRegion. It is the type guard for mesh-processing code. BoundaryMeshRegionQ does the same for boundary meshes.

tools.name: BoundaryMeshRegionQ
tools.description: Tests whether an expression is a valid BoundaryMeshRegion, meaning a closed boundary representation of a solid. It is the check to perform before operations that require watertight geometry. Use it in printing and volume workflows.

tools.name: PLY
tools.description: Polygon File Format used for scanned 3D data, supporting vertex colors and arbitrary per-vertex properties. Import returns Graphics3D or a mesh, and Export writes geometry with colors. Use it for point clouds and scanner output.

tools.name: DXF
tools.description: AutoCAD Drawing Exchange Format for 2D and 3D CAD geometry. Import converts entities into Wolfram Language graphics primitives, and Export writes drawings from graphics. Use it to exchange geometry with CAD systems.

tools.name: MeshCellCount
tools.description: Counts the cells of each dimension in a mesh region, or of a specified dimension. It is the quickest way to gauge mesh size and complexity. Use it to check refinement levels and export cost.

tools.name: DiscretizeGraphics
tools.description: Converts graphics primitives such as Graphics3D scenes, spheres and polygons into a MeshRegion of filled cells. It makes drawn geometry computable, so measures and boolean operations become available. Use it to turn an illustration into an analyzable or printable solid.
tools.notes: Use BoundaryDiscretizeGraphics when only the surface is needed, for example before STL export.

tools.name: BoundaryDiscretizeGraphics
tools.description: Converts graphics primitives into a BoundaryMeshRegion representing only the enclosing surface. It is cheaper than full discretization and produces exactly the watertight representation that STL export and 3D printing require. Use it as the bridge from a drawn scene to a printable file.

tools.name: RegionProduct
tools.description: Forms the Cartesian product of two regions, for example extruding a 2D cross-section along a line to build a prism. It is a convenient way to construct 3D solids from simpler profiles. The resulting region supports all the usual measure and membership operations.
